title: TC0-05357
frame:
Forum: Refugee Appeal Division (appeal tribunal).
Parties: the appellant and the Minister; names are redacted.
Decision under review (from the opening paragraphs): XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX is a citizen of Colombia appealing against the decision of the Refugee Protection Division (RPD) that rejected his claim for asylum.
How the layers nest here: The RAD member is the author (layer 1). The appellant and the Minister make submissions to the RAD (layer 2). The RPD decision under appeal is layer 3, and what the claimant or the Minister said to the RPD, as reported, is layer 4.

paragraphs.text: XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX is a citizen of Colombia appealing against the decision of the Refugee Protection Division (RPD) that rejected his claim for asylum.
XXXX XXXX XXXX fears for his life because he was being extorted by two men who identified themselves as members of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), beginning in 2014.

The RPD accepted XXXX XXXX XXXX allegations, but found that he had a viable internal flight alternative (IFA) in Barranquilla. There was no evidence that the two men who threatened XXXX XXXX XXXX were still members of the FARC, or another armed group, and they only approached him in person in XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. He did receive phone calls in 2016, but these stopped after he changed his phone number. The RPD concluded that the two men who had extorted XXXX XXXX XXXX did not have the means or the motivation to pursue XXXX XXXX XXXX to Barranquilla.

In appeal, XXXX XXXX XXXX argues that the RPD erred in finding that he had an IFA and did not apply the proper test. XXXX XXXX XXXX submits that the RPD member was not sufficiently knowledgeable about the country conditions in Colombia.

The RPD member was correct in her determination that XXXX XXXX XXXX had an IFA in Barranquilla. I confirm the RPD's determination and dismiss this appeal.1 ADMISSIBILITY OF NEW EVIDENCE SUBMITTED ON APPEAL

Within XXXX XXXX XXXX appeal record, he stated that he intended on submitting new evidence that included an affidavit from a co-worker stating that men went to look for him and a letter from his employer referring to the reasoning for relocation. In January 2021, the Refugee Appeal Division (RAD) contacted XXXX XXXX XXXX to ask if he still intended on producing this evidence, and XXXX XXXX XXXX did so on January 27, 2021. This new evidence was submitted after the appeal was perfected, with no submissions.

The following are the documents that were submitted: * Exhibit A: A Word document dated XXXX 2021 and entitled "Case Update News XXXX XXXX" listing six articles and reports, with internet links to the documents. * Exhibit B: A written statement from the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, signed by the leader of payroll and compensation, dated XXXX XXXX XXXX 2021, translated. * Exhibit C: A sworn statement by XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, dated XXXX XXXX XXXX 2021, translated.2 Test for admissibility of new evidence

Subsection 110(4) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA) states that new evidence will only be admitted where that evidence: 1) arose after the rejection of the claim by the RPD; 2) was not reasonably available; or 3) the appellant could not reasonably have been expected in the circumstances to have presented the evidence, at the time of the rejection. I cannot admit new evidence unless it falls under one of these three categories.3
If the new evidence meets one of the above requirements, I must then assess whether the evidence is credible, relevant, and new.4

With respect to the new evidence submitted after the perfection of the appeal, in deciding whether to admit it, I must consider any relevant factors, including those listed in Rule 29(4) of the RAD Rules, such as (i) the document's relevance and probative value and (ii) whether it contains new evidence and (iii) whether XXXX XXXX XXXX, with reasonable effort, could have provided the document with his appeal record.5 Decision on the admissibility of the new evidence
I find that Exhibits A (in part) and B are inadmissible, and that Exhibit C is admissible.

Exhibit A is a list of articles and reports that have not been translated into English. Within the list, the titles of the articles and reports were translated into English; however, the text of all the articles, except one, were in Spanish. The one article that is in English is titled "Overview of Violence Against Social Leaders in Colombia", published by InSight Crime, and is dated February 18, 2020, which post-dates the rejection of XXXX XXXX XXXX claim by the RPD.

As such, the items in Spanish are inadmissible because they do not respect RAD Rule 28(1).6 However, the one article in English post-dates the rejection of XXXX XXXX XXXX claim by the RPD. Thus, it meets one of the criteria of subsection 110(4) of the IRPA. The content of this article is new, not only because it post-dates the rejection of XXXX XXXX XXXX claim, but because it adds information about criminal gangs and violence against social leaders in Colombia that was not part of the RPD record. This topic is relevant to XXXX XXXX XXXX basis of fear of criminal gangs, and the article comes from a credible and independent source that is verifiable. Given the date of the article, XXXX XXXX XXXX, even with reasonable effort, could not have provided it with his appeal record.

For these reasons, I conclude that part of Exhibit A, a media article titled "Overview of Violence Against Social Leaders in Colombia", published by InSight Crime, dated February 18, 2020, is admissible. The rest of Exhibit A is inadmissible.

Exhibit B is a written declaration by the person responsible for payroll for XXXX XXXX XXXX former employer. It post-dates the rejection of XXXX XXXX XXXX claim; however, its content does not. The document states that XXXX XXXX XXXX worked at three different locations and provides the dates up to XXXX XXXX XXXX 2018. It also states that the "reason for his transfer was for security reasons of the employee due to constant threats against him." In my opinion, this information was reasonably available before, and XXXX XXXX XXXX could reasonably have been expected in the circumstances to have presented this evidence before the time of the rejection of his claim. Thus, it does not meet the criteria of subsection 110(4) of the IRPA. For these reasons, Exhibit B is inadmissible.

Exhibit C is a written declaration by XXXX XXXX XXXX former co-worker. It is called a sworn statement, yet it is not actually in the form of a sworn affidavit, before a notary or a commissioner of oaths, it is merely signed by the person making the statement. It post-dates the rejection of XXXX XXXX XXXX claim, and the information contained in it also does. The author states that over the course of 2020, she heard on more than one occasion that a group of men were looking for XXXX XXXX XXXX and that she warned him to be cautious in XXXX of 2020 because according to authorities in the area they are members of an armed group dedicated to extortion and kidnapping. In my opinion, this information was not reasonably available before and XXXX XXXX XXXX could not reasonably have been expected in the circumstances to have presented this evidence before the time of the rejection of his claim. Thus, it does meet the criteria of subsection 110(4) of the IRPA.

The content of this declaration is new, not only because it post-dates the rejection of XXXX XXXX XXXX claim, but because it adds information about the people that XXXX XXXX XXXX fears that was not part of the RPD record. This information is relevant to XXXX XXXX XXXX continued basis of fear of these persons, and although it is not truly a sworn statement, the declaration seems to come from a credible source that is verifiable, with an identification number. Given the date of the declaration, and the timeline of the information in its contents, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX even with reasonable effort, could not have provided it with his appeal record, which was perfected in XXXX of 2020.
For these reasons, Exhibit C is admissible. ANALYSIS OF THE MERITS OF THE APPEAL Standard of review

When reviewing the RPD decision, I am required to independently assess all the evidence and determine whether the RPD was correct in relation to each alleged error of law, fact or mixed fact and law. I may defer to the RPD in the exceptional situation that I find that it had a meaningful advantage in the circumstances, and reasons will be provided in that situation.7 To be clear, this is not the situation in this case. Credibility
The RPD did not make any findings specifically on credibility and accepted XXXX XXXX XXXX allegations, except those issues specifically identified in the IFA analysis.
I see no reason to interfere with this RPD finding and conclude that it is correct. Internal Flight Alternative (IFA) The RPD did not err in assessing the viability of an IFA in Barranquilla

The RPD found that the availability of an IFA in Barranquilla was the determinative issue in this claim. This was explored during the hearing. XXXX XXXX XXXX was asked questions about the topic and his lawyer provided submissions on it in writing.
It is my opinion that the RPD member was correct in her IFA assessment.
XXXX XXXX XXXX does have an IFA in Barranquilla, because, in my opinion, he will not be at risk from the criminals who were extorting him in XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX.

This IFA assessment is based on a two-prong test. Once the IFA has been raised, the onus of proof is on XXXX XXXX XXXX to establish that 1) there is a serious possibility that he will be persecuted in the part of the country identified as an IFA or that on a balance of probabilities, he would be subjected personally to a danger of torture or to a risk to his life or a risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment in the IFA; 2) the conditions in that part of the country must be such that it would be objectively unreasonable or unduly harsh, in all the circumstances, including those particular to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX for him to seek refuge there.8 First prong- The lack of risk faced in Barranquilla

XXXX XXXX XXXX was first approached in XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX in XXXX of 2014 at his place of employment by individuals who identified themselves as members of the FARC. His girlfriend at the time was present when the two men demanded money. He gave them money, but he also reported this extortion to the police, providing a description of the two men. XXXX XXXX XXXX resigned from his job and moved to Bogota, where he is originally from.

XXXX XXXX XXXX was then hired by another company in XXXX of 2015 who asked him to relocate to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and he agreed because it was a good opportunity professionally. In XXXX of 2016, he was once again threatened by the same individuals in XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, this time on his way home. He gave them money again and soon transferred to an office near Bogota.

Starting in XXXX of 2016, he began to receive calls from unknown numbers and the caller would hang up. In XXXX of 2016 he answered a call, and the caller knew his name and said he knew where he was working. The caller said XXXX XXXX XXXX owed them a lot of money and threatened him. XXXX XXXX XXXX believes the caller was one of the men who had previously threatened him. Following this, he changed his number and did not receive any further calls.

In XXXX of 2018, XXXX XXXX XXXX learned from a former co-worker at the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX office of the foundation he worked for that two men had gone to the office looking for him, and the co-worker believed they were gang members. XXXX XXXX XXXX reported this incident to the authorities in XXXX of 2018 and eventually left Colombia on XXXX XXXX XXXX 2018.

While in Canada, XXXX XXXX XXXX was contacted by the police in Colombia who were investigating his complaint and he gave them information about the co-worker who saw the men asking about XXXX XXXX XXXX in 2018. The investigator told XXXX XXXX XXXX that based on some complaints to the police in XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, a FARC financial leader member had been arrested in 2015, and that XXXX XXXX XXXX report from 2014 was one of those complaints.
XXXX XXXX XXXX was asked by the RPD if there was any reason why he could not relocate and live in Barranquilla, and he answered that he would fear for his safety there.

XXXX XXXX XXXX testified that he did not know how he could be found in Barranquilla but that he assumed that his persecutors had influence throughout the entire country, adding that there were guerillas and armed groups all over the country who had ties to politicians and the police.

XXXX XXXX XXXX also testified that despite the two men identifying themselves as FARC members the first time he saw them in 2014, he did not know if they still were, after the demobilization of the FARC in 2016, or if they were part of another armed group.

The RPD acknowledged that there were criminal organizations, such as armed groups, FARC dissidents or the guerilla group ELN that had contacts with police and political spheres, but noted that XXXX XXXX XXXX did not know if his persecutors were still part of an armed group and there was no evidence of this.

The RPD concluded that there was no persuasive evidence that the agents of persecution had the ability to locate and pursue XXXX XXXX XXXX outside of XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX for the following reasons: * XXXX XXXX XXXX had only ever been approached in person in XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, which is hundreds of kilometres from Barranquilla. * The phone calls from unknown callers stopped after he changed his number. * There is no evidence that the two men tried to find XXXX XXXX XXXX between XXXX of 2016 and XXXX of 2018. * In 2018, no one at the office where the two men asked about him gave them information about XXXX XXXX XXXX whereabouts. * There have been no further attempts to find him.

The RPD concluded that XXXX XXXX XXXX agents of persecution's motivation was simply financial, and that they would not be motivated to pursue him to Barranquilla, simply to further extort him, for the following reasons: * XXXX XXXX XXXX was initially approached for extortion, and the two men only ever indicated that they wanted money. * Even if his complaint from 2014 played a role in the arrest of a FARC member, the two men never indicated that they were motivated by anything other than money. * When they accosted him in 2016, which was after the capture, they simply demanded money, as they did in the phone call in XXXX of 2016.

Finally, the RPD referred to the country conditions documentary evidence about the FARC and the peace accord that was signed in 2016, concluding that the recent disarmament of the FARC would have significantly impacted its ability to carry out attacks outside areas of its control, particularly given its significantly decreased numbers. The RPD also found that there was no evidence that there was any significant presence of FARC dissidents in Barranquilla or the surrounding areas.

In appeal, XXXX XXXX XXXX argues that the RPD did not properly identify the test for IFA and quoted a lengthy citation from the Velasquez decision. XXXX XXXX XXXX also argues that the RPD's IFA findings were made without proper analysis of the risk he would face, which constitutes a reviewable error.

XXXX XXXX XXXX submits that the RPD went against her own findings by first accepting his allegations as credible, then acknowledging that there was evidence of criminal organizations in Colombia known to have contacts within the police or political spheres, but still concluding that Barranquilla was a safe place for him.
XXXX XXXX XXXX also cites jurisprudence that stands for the principle that the fact that a proposed IFA was far away would not, without more, constitute a viable IFA.

He goes on to refer to the International Crisis Group that was cited talking about FARC dissident groups and where they operate. XXXX XXXX XXXX argues that sending him to a place where potentially there could be a fraction of armed groups could be deadly. He also refers to the confusion over which Front or subgroup of the FARC his agents of persecution said they were members of. The two men stated they were with the XXXX XXXX and this is how XXXX XXXX XXXX described them in his BOC narrative, but the police report from 2014 refers to the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX lawyer made submissions on this discrepancy and the RPD noted the distinction.

XXXX XXXX XXXX argues that according to the UNHCR, there is no XXXX XXXX XXXX but there is a 40th. XXXX XXXX XXXX submits that the RPD made a mistake about which FARC Front group was in question and that this shows she did not have sufficient knowledge about the country conditions in Colombia to make a proper IFA assessment.

I have reviewed the RPD record about the differing references to the FARC Front the two men first identified with and XXXX XXXX XXXX BOC narrative refers to the XXXX. As such, it was not the RPD's error and, in my opinion, the RPD provided a proper assessment of the country conditions specific to the FARC based on the objective documentary evidence available to her.
In essence, XXXX XXXX XXXX is arguing that because armed groups, including FARC dissidents, operate all over the country, Barranquilla cannot be a viable IFA for him.

In the new evidence that I have admitted as Exhibit C, XXXX XXXX XXXX former co-worker in the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX office states that during 2020, she heard on more than one occasion that a group of men were looking for XXXX XXXX XXXX and that in XXXX of 2020 she warned him to be cautious because according to the authorities in the area they were members of an armed group dedicated to extortion and kidnapping.

In my opinion, the RPD was correct to find that there was insufficient evidence that the two men that extorted XXXX XXXX XXXX were still members of a FARC group, especially after the 2016 peace accord. I also find that there was insufficient evidence that the two men could locate XXXX XXXX XXXX outside of XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX based on how he was contacted after 2014. He was accosted once in person in 2016, in XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, and he received phone calls. These phone calls stopped after he changed his phone number. The only time anyone asked about XXXX XXXX XXXX since was in XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and the local authorities say that the persons asking were members of an armed group dedicated to extortion and kidnapping.
In my opinion, this latest evidence confirms that the men looking for XXXX XXXX XXXX are only interested in extortion, and only in the area of XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX.

Furthermore, XXXX XXXX XXXX wife, who was present the first time the extortion occurred, and from whom he is now separated, was never contacted by the two men, and has never been asked about XXXX XXXX XXXX. I also think it is significant that XXXX XXXX XXXX family still in Colombia has not been contacted or harassed in any way. XXXX XXXX XXXX testified that he was not sure if anyone he worked with in the past had been asked about his whereabouts, and he did not know if anything happened to the other people who made complaints to the police about being extorted in XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX.

With respect to the motivation behind pursuing XXXX XXXX XXXX, he was initially approached for extortion, and the two men only ever indicated that they wanted money. Not once did they refer to his complaint to the police, or to another FARC member being arrested. In my opinion, the only reason XXXX XXXX XXXX was ever contacted and threatened was for extortion purposes and on a balance of probabilities, it has not been established that the two men who extorted him would go all the way to Barranquilla to further extort him.
Finally, the objective documentary evidence shows that there is not a significant, if any, presence of FARC dissidents in the Barranquilla area.9

Based on the above, I agree with the RPD for the same reasons, and conclude that it is correct to say that that there is insufficient evidence that the criminals who extorted XXXX XXXX XXXX in XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX would have the means and the motivation to seek him out in Barranquilla. Second prong-Barranquilla is reasonable
XXXX XXXX XXXX has the onus of demonstrating that the IFA is objectively unreasonable or unduly harsh.

Case law has established a very high threshold when determining whether the proposed IFA is unduly harsh. In Ranganathan, the Federal Court of Appeal states the following: It requires nothing less than the existence of conditions which would jeopardize the life and safety of a claimant in travelling or temporarily relocating to a safe area.10
XXXX XXXX XXXX testified that besides his fear for his safety from the two men who extorted him, there was no other reason why he could not live in Barranquilla.

The RPD noted that XXXX XXXX XXXX was educated and had significant employment experience in Colombia. Also, XXXX XXXX XXXX has resided in various locations in Colombia, including Bogota and XXXX. The RPD also noted that Barranquilla is a large metropolitan city with a population of 2 million people.

The RPD acknowledged that there are some criminal groups in Barranquilla but found that it was speculative to suggest that XXXX XXXX XXXX would become a target of a different criminal organization if he were to return to Colombia.
As such, the RPD concluded that XXXX XXXX XXXX had not met his burden of proving that Barranquilla was an unreasonable place to relocate to.
XXXX XXXX XXXX did not make arguments about the second prong of the IFA test in appeal.
I agree with the RPD for the same reasons and see no reason to interfere with this conclusion.
I have considered XXXX XXXX XXXX personal situation and find that the RPD was correct. XXXX XXXX XXXX failed to prove that it would be objectively unreasonable for him to relocate to Barranquilla.

Having found that Mr. Pulido has a safe and viable IFA in Barranquilla, I confirm the decision of the RPD that XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX is neither a "Convention refugee" nor a "person in need of protection".11

The appeal is dismissed.
